messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 58
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Bomb Disposal Technician
  trauma_type: Child's life-threatening illness
  pcl5: 39

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory (Hospital): Hospital or antiseptic smell, Visual (Needles/Medical): Medical equipment such as needles or drips, Children Present: Being around children
  Threat: Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert, Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Negative Emotions: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
  Memory: Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning, Full Sensory Reliving: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once, Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
  Negative Appraisals: Weakness Belief: I am a weak person, Fear Going Crazy: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Rajiv, a 58-year-old South Asian man and bomb disposal technician, has been grappling with the aftermath of his son’s life-threatening illness that occurred three years ago. His wife had rushed him to the hospital one night when he was just five months old, and Rajiv vividly remembers the sterile antiseptic smell and the frantic pace of the emergency room staff as they rushed around trying to stabilize his newborn. The memory of those days remains seared in his mind, particularly the moments when medical personnel were administering treatments with needles or inserting IV drips. He recalls the fear and helplessness he felt as a parent, unable to do anything but watch and wait. Since then, Rajiv has found himself increasingly sensitive to the antiseptic smell that now serves as an unwelcome reminder of those harrowing moments in the hospital. Rajiv’s occupation as a bomb disposal technician puts him in environments where the threat of danger is always present, yet he finds it difficult to reconcile this professional risk with his personal experience. The fear and physical reactions triggered by the antiseptic smell have begun to bleed into other areas of his life, particularly when around children. He often avoids situations that might expose him to such smells or medical equipment, which has led to a significant reduction in his interactions with his son and extended family. At night, Rajiv struggles to fall asleep due to a persistent sense of needing to stay alert. The idea that he could drift off and miss something important, despite knowing it’s irrational, keeps him awake for hours each night. This sleep disturbance has left him feeling fatigued during the day, which affects his concentration at work. Rajiv also experiences intense negative emotions when triggered by these memories. He often feels overwhelmed with fear, horror, anger, and guilt, as if he is reliving those moments of helplessness all over again. The full sensory reliving of those traumatic events can be so vivid that it feels like they are happening in the present moment, making it difficult for him to distinguish between past and current experiences. His negative appraisals have further compounded his distress. Rajiv has come to believe he is a weak person because he cannot control his reactions or stop bad things from happening to those he loves. He worries that his responses since the event mean he is “going crazy,” which isolates him even more as he struggles to explain these experiences to others, including his wife. The cumulative effect of these symptoms has led Rajiv to seek help now. His sleepless nights and avoidance behaviors have strained his relationship with his family, particularly his wife, who feels increasingly disconnected from him. At work, the difficulty in concentrating has made his job more challenging and stressful, leading to a decline in his performance. What finally brought Rajiv to therapy was an incident at work where he had a strong physical reaction to a faint antiseptic smell, nearly causing him to make a critical error while handling a live bomb. He realized that if he did not address these issues, they could jeopardize both his career and the safety of others. Rajiv hopes for relief from the overwhelming fear and sense of helplessness that have dominated his life since his son’s illness. He is looking for strategies to manage his reactions better and regain a sense of control over his emotions and daily functioning. He wants to reconnect with his family and restore the balance in his professional and personal life, so he can feel more at peace and less burdened by his traumatic memories.
